feat(mac): add Fn tap simulation mode for tap-toggle voice tools

Tap-toggle dictation apps (e.g. Typeless) do not respond to the Fn hold
produced by the HID remapped voice key. This opt-in mode remaps the voice
key to a dropped usage and injects a software Fn tap on voice stream
start/stop instead, so hold-to-speak drives tap-toggle tools end to end.

lifecycle compatibility.

Support ARN9 remote: low-nibble-first ADPCM + BLE name whitelist

The 蓝牙遥控器 2 hardware reporting model number "ARN9" (same VID/PID
0x2717/0x32B8 as RC001/RC003, ATVV v1.0, 16 kHz) was unsupported twice:

- Its BLE advertisement name (小米蓝牙遥控器2 / 2 Pro) is not in the
  approved-name whitelist, so the voice channel never connected.
- Its firmware encodes ADPCM low-nibble-first, while RC001/RC003
  (firmware 2671) encode high-nibble-first; decoding high-first on
  ARN9 audio produces heavy distortion.

Changes:

- IMAADPCMDecoder gains a lowNibbleFirst flag (default false, so
  existing devices are unaffected).
- When the 2A24 model number contains "ARN9", the bridge flips the
  decoder to low-nibble-first and logs it.
- XiaomiRemoteModel.identified maps ARN9 to the RC family so the UI
  badge resolves; BLE name whitelist accepts 小米蓝牙遥控器2 / 2 Pro /
  arn9.

Verified on an ARN9 remote (voice intelligible with low-nibble-first,
distorted without).

fix(mac): correct TV button native keyCode to 10

Real RC003 hardware emits keyCode 10 (ISO section key) for the TV key,
not 50 as mapped since the initial release. The mismatch made
KeyboardEventSuppressor arm the wrong descriptor, leaking a section
sign into the focused input on every TV press in monitored mode.

Evidence: session-level tap measured keyCode 10 with flags 0x100 on 30
consecutive presses; a synthetic keyCode 50 event produces a middle dot,
not a section sign. Only verified on one RC003; other firmware untested.

fix(mac): allow repeated presses for non-repeatable button actions (#255)

A button whose single-click is bound to an action that cannot hold-to-repeat
(custom shortcut, Command combinations, open custom app, preset app launch)
only fired on the first press. Every later press edge was dropped by the
600 ms stable-release latch in HIDRemoteMonitor.shouldAcceptRawPress, and
each dropped press cancelled the pending unlock timer, so rapid tapping
stayed locked out until the button had been released for 600 ms with no new
press edge. Reported in issue #205 and reproduced on 1.9.10 build 136.

The latch itself is correct: per Bugs/2026-08-09-post-fix-multi-remote-hid-routing.md
a single physical hold can produce a spurious release followed by a re-press
449 ms later, which is longer than a deliberate double tap, so no timing
threshold separates a held button from rapid tapping. Removing the latch or
its renewal would bring back the held-button flood fixed on 2026-08-09.

Add a per-button opt-in instead. Default off, so behaviour is unchanged:

- RemoteDeviceMappings gains optional buttonRapidPressEnabled, following the
  buttonApplicationProfileIDs back-compat pattern; old profiles need no
  migration and configuration files without the field import as off.
- AppSettings stores it per button and per remote, persists it, carries it
  through profile switches, export/import and Restore Defaults.
- shouldAcceptRawPress takes allowsRapidPress and clears the latch for that
  button when set. startRepeatIfNeeded is untouched, so the app's own repeat
  timer still never runs for these actions.
- A dropped press now logs reason=awaiting_stable_release instead of being
  silently discarded; this applies regardless of the setting.
- The switch is inline in the single-click editor for actions that cannot
  hold-to-repeat, with help text noting that holding may then repeat.

Verified: swift build, swift test 393 passed, scripts/test.sh 43 passed.
Real RC001/RC003 acceptance is still outstanding; see
Testing/RapidRepeatedButtonPresses.md and the Bugs record for the boundary.

  仍取不到时使用当前指针位置。事件带合成标记，且不经过
  KeyboardEventSuppressor 的按键计数路径。
